title: Student duties: securing your ID and documents, and dressing modestly
keywords: ID, documents, enrollment record, dress code, modest attire, decent, guests dress code, grooming, thesis defense, presentation
text:
Secure all means of identification and proof of enrollment, including the student’s Identification Card (ID), Invoice, Student Enrollment Record (SER), Course Approval Form (CAF), flowchart clearance, and other pertinent documents. For security reasons, enrolled students must present their validated Benilde student ID when entering the campus (See Appendix C Procedures for Securing Temporary Gate Pass and Replacing Lost/Damaged ID).
2.3.5.7 Recognize the sensibilities of others by dressing in accordance with the Campus Dress Code and adhering to conventions of good grooming. Students are expected to be in modest and decent attire, presenting oneself in a manner appropriate to a formal academic learning environment (See Appendix D General and Program Dress Code Policy). Students are required to adhere to the prescribed dress code for their particular discipline or for specific academic functions such as thesis defense, class presentations, reports, and other activities. Students’ guests are likewise covered by the College’s dress code policy.

title: Student duties: facilities, phones on silent, activities end at 9 PM, visitors
keywords: phone, cellphone, silent mode, charging, 9 PM, curfew, visitors, guests, facilities, classroom, chapel, activities
text:
Handle campus facilities/equipment with reasonable care, using these only for the intended purpose. Students are allowed to use the College’s facilities and equipment for business meetings, and social, cultural, and recreational activities subject to regulations governing usage.
2.3.5.9.1 Charging of mobile phones and other electronic communications devices is prohibited except in designated areas.
2.3.5.9.2 Mobile phones and other electronic communications devices must be kept in silent mode inside classrooms, learning resource centers, and chapels. These must be all placed on silent mode during official school functions.
2.3.5.9.3 For the safety and security of all concerned, co-and extracurricular activities on-campus must end at 9:00 p.m., beyond which, prior approval of either the School Dean or the Student Life Dean is required. The presence of faculty and/or an administrator organizer is required for the entire duration of any activity extending beyond the 9:00 p.m. cut-off.
2.3.5.10 Treat all visitors with utmost courtesy. When inviting guests for course-related or extracurricular activities, students should consult their academic chairpersons and/or School Dean, or the Center for Student Life unit heads and/or Dean, respectively.
2.3.5.10.1 Students are expected to coordinate with pertinent offices regarding entry permits, parking arrangements, and related logistics.
2.3.5.10.2 Students have the obligation to brief their visitors on campus decorum. They must inform and obtain from pertinent College authorities an endorsement for offcampus invitational activities. Students may participate as official representatives or delegates of the College only upon approval of the School Dean or the Dean of Student Life.
Conduct that is contrary to the aforementioned norms is detailed in Section 7.7.1 and Section 7.7.2.
Acts of misconduct shall be dealt with accordingly as stipulated in Section 2.2.6 and Section 7.8.

title: Identification cards (Benilde ID policy)
keywords: ID, school ID, student ID, scan ID, wear ID, lanyard, lost ID, damaged ID, invalid ID, temporary pass, ID validation, enter campus, laboratory
text:
Identification Cards (IDs)
3.3.1 Issuance of ID The College issues each student an Identification Card (ID) upon enrollment to the College. The ID is validated on a per-term basis upon confirmation of enrollment for the term.
In cases when there is a delay in the issuance and/or printing of ID cards, the Office of the Registrar (RO) shall issue a temporary pass indicating specific validity. In such cases, the temporary pass is treated as their proof of identification.
3.3.2 ID Validation The Finance Office validates the ID upon payment of enrollment fees for the term. A valid ID entitles the bearer access to the campuses, and the rights and privileges of a bona fide student. Nonpayment of enrollment fees renders the ID invalid (See Appendix C Procedures for Securing Temporary Gate Pass and Replacing Lost/ Damaged ID).
3.3.3 Benilde ID Policy Students must scan their ID upon entering and must wear it at all times while inside the campus, except when in the laboratory.
Students entering the campus without an ID will be recorded an infraction through the designated QR code at the entrances. (See Section 7.7.1.14.3).
In cases where a student’s ID is damaged or defaced, deemed invalid, or lost, the following procedures shall apply:
3.3.3.1 Students with a damaged or defaced ID shall be referred to the RO for ID replacement by the Center for Emergency, Safety, and Security (CEMSS).
3.3.3.2 Students with an ID deemed invalid because of unsettled accounts shall be referred to the Finance Office for accounts updating by the CEMSS.
3.3.3.3 Students with a lost ID shall be referred to the Center for Restorative Discipline (CRD) by the Center for Emergency, Safety, and Security (CEMSS) for processing.

title: Attendance: absences, tardiness, cutting class and failing due to absences
keywords: attendance, absent, absence, late, tardy, tardiness, cutting class, leaving early, 20 minutes, half absence, failing grade, R, F, excessive absences, dropout, how many absences, 20% of course hours
text:
Attendance
5.6.1 Regardless of academic standing, students who incur absences of more than 20% of the total course hours get a failing grade (R) or (F) and will earn no credits for the course.
5.6.2 Students must regularly and punctually attend all class meetings in all their courses.
5.6.3 Absences. Students shall be marked absent if they arrive after
5.6.3.1 The first 20 minutes of a 1-hour class; or
5.6.3.2 The first 30 minutes of a 1.5-hour (or longer) class.
5.6.4 Tardiness Students shall be considered late, which is considered a halfabsence, if they arrive in class within:
5.6.4.1 The first 20 minutes of a 1-hour class; or
5.6.4.2 The first 30 minutes of a 1.5-hour (or longer) class.
5.6.5 Cutting class Student leaving without the teacher’s permission will result in the student being marked absent or late based on the quality of attendance, including arriving significantly late or leaving early without valid reason.
5.6.6 Excessive absence is not a valid reason for withdrawal.
5.6.7 Students shall receive a failing grade (failure due to excessive absences) if they incur:
5.6.7.1 Six (6) or more absences in a class conducted two (2) times a week; or
5.6.7.2 Three (3) or more absences in a class conducted once a week; or
5.6.7.3 Three (3) or more absences in laboratory or modular classes (for SHRIM and SDA students).

title: Approved absences for official College activities
keywords: approved absence, official activity, excused, excuse, approved absence form, school event, representative, dean
text:
Absences Due to Participation in Official Activities
5.6.9.1 Approvals for absences must come from either of the following persons:
5.6.9.1.1 the School Dean for academic activities; or
5.6.9.1.2 the Student Life Dean for non-academic/ co-curricular/ extracurricular activities and CSBLIFE-, CSBGRAD-, or NSTP-related activities
5.6.9.2 Approved absences shall not be counted against students nor regarded as part of the number of allowable absences (See Section 5.6). Students shall be allowed to make up for missed quizzes, examinations, graded recitations, assignments, seatwork, and other activities or requirements at the soonest possible time.

title: Jurisdiction over students (on campus, off campus and online)
keywords: jurisdiction, off campus, outside school, online, social media, after school hours, weekend, BigSky
text:
Jurisdiction of Benilde over Students The College has jurisdiction over its students while they are on campus premises.
The College also has jurisdiction over its students for acts committed outside its premises and beyond school hours in the following situations:
7.4.1 In cases of violations of College policies or regulations offcampus, even during non-College-sponsored activities and including acts committed online.
7.4.2 In cases where the misconduct of the student involves his or her status as a student or affects the good name or reputation of the College, including in BigSky and other social media platforms.

title: Intellectual property offenses (copying, piracy, plagiarism, AI misuse)
keywords: intellectual property, copyright, piracy, pirated, plagiarism, plagiarize, copying, AI misuse, ChatGPT, photocopy, software piracy, citing, credit
text:
MAJOR OFFENSE (Section 7.8.2), category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies. Sanctions for major offenses are in Section 7.9.1.
Commission of any act constituting an “intellectual property offense” under the College’s Intellectual Property (IP) Rights Policy and Implementing Rules and Regulations 2018-2021 (IPR Policy and IRR available at https://ip.benilde.edu.ph/policy).
7.8.2.20.1 Unauthorized reproduction, including photocopying or any manner of copying, exhibit, use, or distribution, of any printed matter in whole or in part, including software and multimedia presentations, without permission of the author/creator/owner of the intellectual property, subject to the Use Rights under the IP Rights Policy, fair use principles for copyrighted works, and other exceptions provided in the Code.
7.8.2.20.2 Use, distribution, transfer, rental, sale, or production of counterfeit, unlicensed, or pirated intellectual property contained in an optical media as defined in R.A. No. 9239.
7.8.2.20.3 Deliberate failure to comply with the disclosure and manifestation requirements of the IPR Policy and IRR.
7.8.2.20.4 Failure to disclose, identify, or cite co-authors, co-creators or co-inventors in a research, creative work, or invention despite knowledge of the identities and contributions of these persons.
7.8.2.20.5 Unauthorized use, distribution, transfer, rental, sale or production of Benilde IP and merchandise bearing Benilde marks.
7.8.2.20.6 Non-compliance to the usage policy and institutional styleguide for Benilde marks.
7.8.2.20.7 Plagiarism and acts constituting academic dishonesty, including violations related to the misuse of AI tools, such as but not limited to: failing to disclose AI use when required, submitting AI-generated content as one’s own, falsifying AI declarations, or using AI to circumvent learning.
7.8.2.20.8 Violation of the right of authors, inventors, and creators to the integrity of their work in the exercise of use rights and fair use.
7.8.2.20.9 Failure of any person to cite or acknowledge the College in inventions and works: (a) developed or produced with the substantial use of College resources; (b) receiving grants or incentives from or funded through the College; or (c) when the College assigned, released, or waived its intellectual property rights in favor of such person
7.8.2.20.10 Knowingly aiding or abetting anyone; or failure to report anyone who commits intellectual property offenses.
7.8.2.20.11 Violation of the provision on confidentiality under Rule 12 of the IPR Policy IRR.
7.8.2.20.12 All other acts analogous to the foregoing.

title: Data Privacy Act violations (sharing others' personal information)
keywords: data privacy, personal information, doxxing, sharing personal data, consent, private information, screenshot
text:
MAJOR OFFENSE (Section 7.8.2), category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies. Sanctions for major offenses are in Section 7.9.1.
Commission of any act violating R.A. No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012 and the DLS-CSB Data Privacy policy:
7.8.2.21.1 Accessing/processing/divulging personal information of others without consent.
7.8.2.21.2 Selling personal information that they are in possession of or they have access to.
7.8.2.21.3 Using or disclosing personal information collected through College activities/events or service for profiling.

title: Cheating and academic dishonesty (including AI misuse)
keywords: cheating, cheat, copy, copying, plagiarism, exam, examination, notes, leaking, AI, ChatGPT, answers, take exam for another, academic dishonesty, crib notes, cellphone during exam, kopya
text:
MAJOR OFFENSE (Section 7.8.2), category: Offenses against Good Morals and Norms of Decency. Sanctions for major offenses are in Section 7.9.1.
Acts of cheating such as, but not limited to, the following:
A. Unauthorized possession of notes or any material relevant to an examination, whether or not the student actually uses them during the examination.
B. Looking at examination papers of others and/or allowing another to glance/look at one’s own paper/notes during examination.
C. Copying or allowing another to copy from one’s examination papers, assigned reports, case analyses, reaction papers, theses, and other similar materials.
D. Communicating with another during examinations without permission from the teacher or proctor.
E. Furnishing another person with answers to examination questions.
F. Leaking examination questions to other students.
G. Unauthorized use of cellular phones, communication gadgets, or any electronic device during examinations and other academic activity.
H. Plagiarism, defined as intentionally or knowingly representing as one’s own work another person’s ideas, data, or language in any academic endeavor or exercise without proper acknowledgement.
I. Misuse of AI tools, such as, but not limited to, failing to disclose AI use when required, submitting AI-generated content as one’s own, falsifying AI declarations, or using AI to circumvent learning.
J. Taking an examination for another student, in which case both parties shall be liable.
K. Infringement of the Intellectual Property Policy and its IRR. (See Section 7.8.2.20)
L. Other acts of academic dishonesty committed online.

title: Sanctions for major offenses (probation, suspension, exclusion, expulsion)
keywords: penalty, punishment, sanction, suspension, expulsion, exclusion, probation, consequences, what happens, major offense, scholarship, formation, in-school service, records
text:
Sanctions for Major Offenses Any or a combination of the following disciplinary actions for major offenses may be imposed on the student:
7.9.1.1 Loss of privileges, such as loss of scholarship/ student aid.
7.9.1.2 Discipline probation, where the student is required to adhere to the provisions of the Discipline Probation Contract.
7.9.1.3 Holding of records (that is, the student will not be allowed access to them).
7.9.1.4 Revocation of degree previously conferred; non- conferment of degree; deferral or withholding of degree, diploma, and/or certificate.
7.9.1.5 Nullification or the cancellation and invalidation of enrollment in the College.
7.9.1.6 The three (3) categories of disciplinary administrative sanctions for serious offenses or violation of school rules and regulations that may be applied upon erring students are: suspension, exclusion, and expulsion.
Article XIV, section 77 of the Manual of Regulations for Private Schools delineate the “Categories of Administrative Penalties”, thus:
7.9.1.6.1 Suspension Suspension is a penalty in which the school is allowed to deny or deprive erring students of attendance in classes for a period not exceeding 20% of the prescribed class days for the academic year or term.
Students under disciplinary suspension are considered on forced leave status and are automatically dropped from the enrollment list.
The decision of the school on every case involving the penalty of suspension which exceeds 20% of the prescribed school days for a school year or term shall be forwarded to the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Regional Office concerned within 10 days from the termination of the investigation of each case for its information.
A student under investigation in a case involving the penalty of expulsion may be placed under preventive suspension and barred from entering the school premises if there is sufficient basis to believe that the continued stay of the student during the period of the investigation constitutes a distraction to the normal operation of the school or poses a risk or danger to the life or persons and property in the school. (See Section 7.9.3)
7.9.1.6.2 Exclusion Exclusion is a penalty in which the school is allowed to exclude or drop the name of the erring student from the school rolls for being undesirable, in which case transfer credentials are immediately issued. A summary investigation shall have been conducted, and no prior approval by the CHED is required in the imposition of the penalty. The decision of the school on every case involving the penalty of exclusion from the rolls together with all the pertinent papers shall, therefore, be led in the school for a period of one year to afford the CHED the opportunity to review the case in the event an appeal is taken by the party concerned.
7.9.1.6.3 Expulsion Expulsion is an extreme penalty on erring students consisting of their exclusion from admission to any public or private school in the Philippines. This requires the prior approval of the CHED Chairperson. The penalty may be imposed for acts or offenses constituting gross misconduct, dishonesty, hazing, carrying deadly weapons, immorality, and selling and/or possession of prohibited drugs such as marijuana. It is also imposed on students exhibiting drug dependency, and for drunkenness, hooliganism, vandalism, forging or tampering with school records or school forms, and other serious school offenses such as assaulting other students or school personnel, instigating illegal strikes, or similar concerted actions resulting in the disruption of activities. Any other acts that cause the stoppage of classes or that prevent any other student or school personnel from entering the school premises and attending classes or discharging their duties will also warrant expulsion. The decision of the school on every case involving the penalty of expulsion together with the supporting papers shall be forwarded to the CHED Regional Office concerned within 10 days of the termination of the investigation of each case.
7.9.1.7 Other Penalties Any of the above sanctions, except expulsion or exclusion, may require a student to undergo the Center for Restorative Discipline Formation Program; render in-school service; or be imposed sanctions, which shall be determined by the Discipline Board, or the CRD Director, as the case may be.
7.9.1.8 Other consequences that may be meted out for major offenses that may be considered less serious:
A. Participation in projects or activities that aim to promote discipline on campus.
B. In-school service, defined as a designated number of hours of volunteer or service/work to the College( a student may be offered an opportunity to complete a specified number of hours of work in lieu of other sanctions).
C. Compliance with educational requirements such as completion of specific seminars/ workshops required by CRD.
D. Any other sanctions that may be deemed appropriate by the CRD Director/Board, whichever may decide the case.

title: Teacher's prerogative on cases of cheating
keywords: cheating, grade R, failing mark, quiz, major exam, caught cheating, honors, admission
text:
Teacher’s Prerogative on Cases of Cheating
7.9.4.1 Students caught cheating on major exams (midterms and finals) and/or major academic requirements may be given a grade of R by the faculty concerned, as provided under Section 7.8.2.45.
Students caught cheating on quizzes, seat works, and other academic activities may be given an outright failing mark on the particular activity.
In both cases mentioned above, the following must be observed:
A. The faculty concerned secures a written admission from the student concerned. SDEAS students may submit their admission through video and transcription.
B. The faculty concerned filed a report to the Center for Restorative Discipline for documentation and reference purposes within five (5) school days of knowing or witnessing the incident.
7.9.4.2 If the student denies the cheating allegation, the faculty may file a written complaint to CRD together with the material evidence or written testimony of witnesses, within five (5) school days of the knowing or witnessing the incident, if possible.
7.9.4.3 The student concerned shall at all times be granted the right to answer the charges against him in writing and have access to evidence therein.
7.9.4.4 The CRD shall determine if the complaint filed should be decided upon summarily by the CRD Director or be endorsed for further investigation to the Discipline Board. The faculty concerned shall then wait for further advice from CRD.
7.9.4.5 If the act of cheating on any academic requirements is repeated and was admitted, CRD will file the complaint accordingly.
7.9.4.6 A student who has been found responsible for academic dishonesty is disqualified from graduating with honors.

title: Temporary gate pass and replacing a lost or damaged ID
keywords: temporary gate pass, forgot ID, lost ID, damaged ID, replace ID, affidavit of loss, CRD, registrar, entry form, false information about ID, ID picture, business attire ID photo
text:
Benilde issues an official identification card (ID) with a computer-registered student number to all enrolled students. The ID is valid for the entire term a student is enrolled in the College. Students must present their ID when entering the campus.
1. A student who fails to present his Benilde ID shall be issued a Temporary Gate Pass after complying with the following procedure:
1.1 Presentation of any of the following documents upon entry: Enrollment Assessment Form (EAF), Official Receipt (OR), or any other valid ID; and
1.2 Completion of an Entry Form (Referral Form 1) and signing of the entry log sheet at the gate. The student shall be accompanied by the security officer to the Center for Restorative Discipline (CRD) for issuance of a Temporary Gate Pass.
2. In the case of an invalid or expired ID due to incomplete medical requirements:
2.1 The student must visit the clinic, where the nurse on duty will explain the details of the missing medical requirements.
2.2 Afterward, the student will need to scan a QR code to receive a temporary gate pass, which is valid for up to one week. This gate pass will be sent directly to the student’s Benilde email account and must be presented to security personnel upon entering the campus.
2.3 The student’s ID will remain invalid or expired until all medical clearance requirements are completed.
Please note that students whose IDs are on hold by the clinic due to other medical concerns will not be issued a temporary gate pass, as their cases are considered urgent
3. In case of ID loss, the student must:
3.1 Secure a clearance and a payment slip for ID replacement from the CRD.
The CRD shall require a student to present an Affidavit of Loss before issuing the clearance;
3.2 Proceed to the Finance Office for payment; and
3.3 Present the following documents to the Registrar’s Office for ID processing:
Clearance Form duly signed by authorized personnel of the CRD and the Br.
Fidelis Leddy Center for Learning Resources (CLR); and Official Receipt.
4. In case of ID loss because of theft, robbery, or other similar incidents, the student must:
4.1 Submit a police/barangay report of the incident to the CRD (consideration will be given to the student).
4.2 Secure a new ID following the procedures in item no. 3
5. To replace a damaged or defaced ID, a student must:
5.1 Secure a Payment Slip from the Registrar’s Office;
5.2 Proceed to the Finance Office for payment; and
5.3 Present the following to the Office of the Registrar for ID processing:
• Old ID (to be surrendered); and
• Official Receipt
6. A student who shifted to another degree program must have his/her ID replaced. The student must:
6.1 Secure a Payment Slip from the Office of the Registrar;
6.2 Proceed to the Finance Office for payment; and
6.3 Present the following to the Office of the Registrar for ID processing:
1. Old ID (to be surrendered)
2. Official Receipt
3. Current SER
7. A student must be in business attire during the ID picture taking. T-shirts (with or without collars) are not acceptable attire for ID picture-taking. A student has the option to have his/her picture retaken or an old ID picture reprinted. The new ID may be claimed from the Office of the Registrar within one (1) working day upon surrendering the Temporary Gate Pass.
8. A student found responsible for giving false information regarding his/her ID shall be charged with a major offense. (See Section 7.8.2.3).
9. The student ID is the property of the College. It must be surrendered upon separation from the College.

title: General Dress Code Policy (tops, bottoms, footwear)
keywords: dress code, attire, uniform, clothes, clothing, skirt, short skirt, mini skirt, shorts, dress, hemline, length, knee, crop top, sleeveless, tank top, revealing, see-through, tight, ripped, torn, slippers, rubber slippers, footwear, shoes, what to wear, wearing, undergarments, midsection
text:
Rationale
The College aims to create an inclusive and supportive learning environment for all students. To uphold this, a dress code that meets current student needs is in place, allowing for self-expression while promoting safety and respect on campus.
The dress code stresses fairness, respect for individuality, and the importance of keeping a focused learning atmosphere. Students are expected to wear clothing that does not disrupt classes or pose safety risks, as determined by the College.
Any student wearing clothing that disrupts learning or compromises safety may be asked to change. Refusal to comply may lead to disciplinary action. The College hopes to instill in students an understanding of and adherence to appropriate dress for a professional environment as they prepare for their future career.
These guidelines are not exhaustive, and the College reserves the authority to decide what clothing is disruptive or unsafe.
General Guidelines
• This policy applies equally to all students, regardless of gender identity. When uncertain about clothing appropriateness, it’s best to refrain from wearing the item.
• Religious clothing/garments associated with religious practices are permitted.
• See-through or overly revealing garments are prohibited. Fabrics that are too tight are also prohibited.
Dress Code Guidelines – Tops, Bottoms, and Footwear
1. Tops
• Crop tops are allowed, provided that no more than two (2) inches of skin are exposed between the top and bottom garment.
• Tops must not reveal undergarments, midsection, torso, back, chest, or breasts.
• If sleeveless, shoulder straps must be at least one (1) inch wide, and the neckline and armholes should be designed to avoid exposing undergarments.
2. Bottoms
• Skirts, shorts, and dresses must extend to at least the midpoint between the natural waistline and the knee.
• Torn, ripped, or slashed fabrics are acceptable provided that any openings or tears are located below this required midpoint and do not expose undergarments.
3. Shoes/Footwear
• Footwear must not detract from or interfere with the learning environment, nor present a safety or health hazard.
• Thong-type rubber slippers are not permitted.
[Note: SHRIM students also follow the separate SHRIM Student Dress Code and Grooming Policy (Appendix D1), which is not included in Tala's handbook.]

title: SMIT, SDG and SDEAS dress code (eXtraOrdinary Mondays, business attire)
keywords: SMIT, SDG, SDEAS, eXtraOrdinary Monday, business attire, first Monday, cross-dressing, polo, barong, blazer, skirt length, shoes, program dress code
text:
Rationale
The School of Deaf Education and Applied Studies (SDEAS), School of Diplomacy and Governance (SDG), and School of Management and Information Technology (SMIT) of De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde acknowledge the need for impression management. Projecting a professional image is an important skill which needs to be developed among students. Knowing how to dress in the corporate world will prepare students to make the desired impression which will help in establishing interpersonal relations and professional networks.
eXtraOrdinary Monday Guidelines
1. The first Monday of every month is designated as eXtraOrdinary Mondays for SDEAS, SDG, and SMIT students.
2. All SDEAS, SDG, and SMIT students are required to be in business attire on eXtraOrdinary Mondays.
3. In the event that the first Monday of the month falls on the midterm or final exam week or on a declared holiday, eXtraOrdinary Mondays would be waived.
General Guidelines
1. SDEAS students are expected to adhere to Benilde’s General Dress Code on all school days, except on eXtraOrdinary Mondays and on the third Monday of every month (when they must be in business attire).
2. SDG students must wear smart casual attire from Mondays to Wednesdays.
They are expected to adhere to Benilde’s General Dress Code on the rest of their school days, except on eXtraOrdinary Mondays (when they must be in business attire).
3. SMIT students are expected to adhere to Benilde’s General Dress Code on all school days, except on eXtraOrdinary Mondays (when they must be in business attire).
4. The wearing of sports attire is not allowed inside the classrooms outside of P.E. class time.
5. SDEAS, SDG, and SMIT are one with the College in highlighting the need to maintain professionalism at ALL times. Faculty and personnel are requested to remind students that the initiative to form students’ sense of dressing shall be applied to all male and female students, regardless of sexual orientation. To preserve the integrity of this policy, cross-dressing, defined as the wearing of attire (clothing, accessories, and shoes, etc.) designed for the opposite sex, is not encouraged. All students of SDEAS, SDG, and SMIT will follow the no cross-dressing policy on all school days, including eXtraOrdinary Mondays.
Business Attire Guidelines for Males
Option 1
• Long-sleeved office polo with collar, in solid color or pinstripes (acceptable colors are white, black, pastel, and earth tone neutrals)
• Coat preferred but not required, in solid color or pinstripes only (no loud prints or torn hems or seams)
• Necktie, in solid colors or pinstripes only (no cartoons or large and loud patterns)
Option 2
• Long-sleeved office barong with short- or long-sleeved white undershirt
• Vests, cardigans, or sweaters in neutral colors allowed (no sports jackets or hoodies)
• Pants: black or blue, straight cut only (no fit or skin-tight pants/trousers and no khaki or printed pants)
• Shoes: black or brown closed leather shoes (no topsiders)
• Belt: leather belt matching the color of shoes
• Socks: office dress socks (no ankle or sports socks)
• Accessories: no earrings, caps, and bonnets
• Hair: neat and tamed (long hair should be tied back)
Business Attire Guidelines for Females
Option 1
• Business attire skirt/dress (straightcut, pencil cut,or A-line), with maximum length of two inches from the knees
Option 2
• For slacks: straight cut (No fit or skin-tight pants/ trousers)
• Collared blazer, in solid color or pinstripes (no loud prints,
• embellishments, or torn seams; no sports jackets or hoodies)
• Shoes: office shoes, closed toe or peep-toe, with at least one-inch heels (no platform heels, wedges, flat shoes, or open-toe shoes)
• Stockings: optional, in solid skin-tone or black colors only
• Accessories: optional (no dangling earrings, caps, and bonnets)
• Hair: tied back or brushed back from the face
• Makeup: optional (minimal to moderate amounts encouraged)

title: Dress code for special occasions, gatherings and school activities
keywords: special occasion, costume, play, performance, graduation attire, school activity, CRD clearance, event dress code
text:
Students are expected to dress appropriately, in accordance with established norms of decency, during special occasions or gatherings and other school- or College-sponsored activities.
Clearance must be secured from the Center for Restorative Discipline (CRD) should students need to wear certain attires for a specific purpose (e.g. costume for play or performances).
For graduation ceremonies, the following is the required attire for students and guests:
For Men
Slacks and a long-sleeved shirt with a tie; barong.
For Women
Dress or skirt, blouse, and formal shoes (with not-too-high heels).
